memory_update.text: FORM should remain a high-priority underfollowed HBM sub-supplier candidate because it has direct HBM probe-card and known-good-die test exposure with company-disclosed HBM revenue growth.
CAMT should remain in the HBM advanced-packaging discovery lane due to direct HBM manufacturer and OSAT order evidence dated June 5, 2026.
ONTO should remain in the discovery lane because it has a disclosed over-$240M HBM manufacturer agreement for 2D inspection and 3D bump metrology through 2027.

KLIC is a plausible but weaker HBM bonding-tool candidate; next layer must verify actual HBM customer qualifications and the share of revenue from thermocompression bonding or other advanced-packaging tools.

For this node, the highest-quality US-listed evidence currently clusters around probe cards, inspection/metrology, 3D bump metrology, and thermocompression bonding rather than memory producers themselves.

node: HBM and advanced-packaging sub-suppliers one or two layers below memory producers
summary: Layer 1B expands the US-listed universe around the HBM advanced-packaging sub-supplier node. The strongest underfollowed lane candidates found in this pass are not memory producers, but test/probe, inspection/metrology, and bonding-equipment suppliers whose products become more critical as HBM stack complexity, known-good-die requirements, TSV/microbump density, and advanced-packaging yield pressure rise. Reference context remains NVIDIA/AMD/TSMC/SK hynix/Samsung/Micron, but the discovery lane prioritizes FORM, CAMT, ONTO, and KLIC. These are research candidates only, not recommendations.
